message.content: {"calls": [{"tool": "chest_xray_classifier", "source_filename": "figures/16582/figure_1a.jpg", "reason": "To detect and localize pulmonary opacities (e.g., peripheral vs central, upper vs lower lobe) on the PA view to match EGPA-associated patterns."}, {"tool": "chest_xray_report_generator", "source_filename": "figures/16582/figure_1a.jpg", "reason": "To obtain a natural language description of opacity distribution, margins, and associated findings (e.g., effusion, lymphadenopathy) that may not be captured by categorical classifier scores."}], "reason": "EGPA typically presents with transient, peripheral, non-segmental opacities often in upper or mid zones; distinguishing this from other options requires precise localization and characterization. The classifier can flag opacity presence/location, while the report generator provides descriptive context (e.g., 'peripheral', 'apical', 'reticulonodular') critical for matching clinical-radiological criteria. Both tools are applied to Figure 1a as it is the standard PA projection best suited for assessing lobar distribution and symmetry. Figure 1b (lateral) is less informative for lobar assignment without prior correlation and is deferred unless initial results are ambiguous."}
